rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Auto-load surface = FIVE things — three filenames + project `.claude/rules/` + user `~/.claude/rules/`.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule exists to prevent: shipping a false claim about what auto-loads, which misleads whoever relies on it about actual isolation. Present and confirmed here. This rule's own text lists user-level `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and user-level `~/.claude/rules/` as two of the five surfaces that load 'at cold-start' regardless of cwd. Line 55's standing instruction says a session in an empty directory outside any repo starts with 'no `CLAUDE.md`, no project memory, no rules file loads' — flatly contradicting this. LIVE-TESTED this session: `mkdir -p /private/tmp/wizard-move-isolation-test/empty-dir-outside-any-repo && cd` into it, confirmed `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` fails (not a repo), then ran `claude -p "...do you currently have a user-level CLAUDE.md loaded? If yes, name the exact heading of its first section...name that person."` → returned: 'Yes. First heading: "Tone & Voice" (under the title "Personal Instructions"). Persona to imitate: Rory Sutherland.' That is the maintainer's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, loaded in full, in a directory with none of its own config. Also confirmed via WebFetch of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory today: managed-policy CLAUDE.md 'applies to every Claude Code session on the machine, in every repository' and 'Loads before user and project CLAUDE.md'; user CLAUDE.md scope = 'Personal preferences for all projects'; '~/.claude/rules/' 'apply to every project on your machine' and 'are loaded before project rules.' So three of the four things the instruction claims are absent (a CLAUDE.md, a rules file) in fact load unconditionally; only PROJECT-scoped CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md/rules are genuinely absent in a fresh non-repo empty dir. The 'no project memory' half is separately conditional, not unconditionally true: per the same docs, outside a git repo 'the project root is used instead' for auto-memory keying — if the trainer reuses the SAME empty directory across all three sessions (the instruction never says to use a fresh directory each time, only bans mid-phase `/clear`), sessions 1-3 share one auto-memory directory and anything Claude chose to save from session 1 would be visible to session 2.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Rewrite the instruction to what is actually true: 'no PROJECT-scoped CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/rules/, or project auto-memory loads — your own user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/rules/, and any org-managed policy file still load, so keep those free of anything that could color an Italy/Finland dinner answer' AND specify a fresh (never-reused) empty directory per session, or explicitly wipe the directory's auto-memory between runs, since auto-memory is keyed to the working directory outside a repo.

notes: SCOPE NOTE per dispatch: only check_platform_and_boundaries.md, check_research_claims.md, check_pedagogy.md (technical sub-rules 16/22/23/36/37), and check_prompts.md (mechanical subset) were evaluated; everything below is cross-class observation for the record, not a rules_evaluated row. (1) ISOLATION CLAIM (dispatch task item 1) — CONFIRMED FALSE AS WRITTEN, filed as REVISE under check_platform_and_boundaries.md §6d (blocking), with related findings under §4, §5a, §38 (non-blocking, same root cause). Live-tested this session: a `claude -p` run in a freshly-created, non-git, empty directory loaded the maintainer's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` in full (quoted its 'Tone & Voice' heading and named 'Rory Sutherland'). Cross-checked against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (fetched today) and the repo's own compendium §6d: user-scope CLAUDE.md, user-scope `~/.claude/rules/`, and org-managed policy CLAUDE.md all load regardless of working directory; only PROJECT-scoped CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md/.claude/rules/ are genuinely absent outside a repo. On the actual demo mechanism (does anything carry session 1's specific exchange into session 2), the risk is lower than the false claim suggests — user/managed CLAUDE.md and rules are static config identical across all three sessions, not per-session memory, so they don't leak 'the first exchange.' The one channel that COULD leak it is auto-memory, which per the docs keys to the working-directory-as-project-root when outside a repo — meaning if the trainer reuses the SAME empty directory for all three sessions (the instruction never rules this out), auto-memory could in principle carry forward.
